observations: Torah 78 is a compact, thematically unified teaching centered on a single master concept: the stratum of reality that precedes Torah-obligation, in which the world is sustained by pure divine grace (matnat chinam / chesed chinam), embodied in the Ten Utterances of Creation. Every bechina relationship in both the dataset and the source text flows back to this single domain. Even the concepts proposed as additions in the additions file (ish pashut, derech eretz, Eretz Yisrael, koach ma'asav, yishuv ha-olam, aseret ha-dibrot, the tzaddik ha-emet) are all expressions of this same pre-Torah, grace-based reality — they do not form independent domains. There is no evil-mirror structure in this Torah: the text does not develop a counterpart cluster of negative/sitra-achra concepts in bechina terms. The one mention of a negative dimension ('all suffering and the grasp of the sitra achra is in the dimension of time') appears in the notes appended from Rebbe Nachman's own manuscript (the editorial appendix at the end), and is framed as an eitza observation about what afflicts people in time — not a bechina cluster. The teaching is positive throughout, focusing entirely on how the tzaddik and the simple person draw life-force from the hidden Torah in the Ten Utterances. One package exhausts the bechina structure of this Torah.
